parts.markdown:
Use our free **Indiana paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Indiana state income tax, county income taxes, Social Security, Medicare and other payroll deductions.

Enter your salary or hourly wage, select your pay frequency and provide your withholding amounts to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Indiana's county income tax system means that employees earning identical salaries may receive different take-home pay depending on where they reside or work.

Whether you work in Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Bloomington, South Bend or another Indiana community, this calculator can help you evaluate employment opportunities and manage your finances.

## How to Use the Indiana Paycheck Calculator

Choose whether you receive an annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross compensation before taxes and deductions. Hourly employees should include their regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal, Indiana and applicable county income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions, healthcare premiums, additional withholding and other employee deductions.

Review the results to understand how each deduction affects your estimated net income.

For the most accurate estimate, refer to your latest payroll statement and Indiana Form WH-4.

parts.markdown:
County income tax is an important component of Indiana paycheck calculations. Ignoring it can result in an estimate that overstates your actual take-home pay.

The [Indiana Department of Revenue](https://www.in.gov/dor/) provides official state and county withholding guidance.

## How Indiana State Income Tax Works

Indiana uses a flat individual income tax rate.

For 2026, the state income tax rate is 2.95%. This rate is scheduled to decrease to 2.90% in 2027.

The state withholding calculation accounts for qualifying employee exemptions before applying the applicable tax rate.

For example, suppose an employee receives $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages and claims one qualifying annual personal exemption of $1,000.

The exemption adjustment per paycheck is approximately $38.46.

Estimated Indiana withholding is therefore:

($2,500 − $38.46) × 2.95% = $72.62

This calculation does not include county income tax or additional withholding.

Review the [Indiana income tax rates](https://secure.in.gov/dor/resources/tax-rates-and-reports/rates-fees-and-penalties/) for official tax-year information.

## Understanding Indiana County Income Taxes

Indiana's local income tax system operates at the county level.

The applicable county tax generally depends on where an employee lived on January 1 of the tax year. For qualifying nonresidents, the principal Indiana employment or business location on that date may determine the applicable county tax.

Consequently, moving to a different county during the year does not necessarily mean that your payroll department should immediately switch your county withholding rate.

County tax rates may also change during the calendar year.

### Selected Indiana county tax rates

These examples illustrate why using a statewide average county tax rate would not provide a reliable paycheck estimate.

Consult Indiana's official [Departmental Notice #1](https://www.in.gov/dor/files/dn01.pdf) for the complete county tax schedule and applicable effective dates.

## Indiana County Tax Calculation Example

Assume an employee receives $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages, claims one applicable $1,000 annual exemption and is subject to Allen County's 1.59% income tax rate.

Adjusted biweekly taxable wages:

$2,500 − $38.46 = $2,461.54

State income tax:

$2,461.54 × 2.95% = $72.62

County income tax:

$2,461.54 × 1.59% = $39.14

Combined state and county withholding:

$72.62 + $39.14 = $111.76

An employee subject to a different county rate could have a different withholding amount despite receiving the same salary.

## Understanding Indiana Form WH-4

Indiana employees provide state withholding information using Form WH-4.

The form records personal exemptions, qualifying dependent exemptions and information used to determine the applicable county tax.

Certain dependent exemptions can provide additional withholding adjustments, including allowances for eligible first-time dependent claims and qualifying adopted children.

The exact exemption amount depends on the employee's circumstances and the applicable instructions.

Review your withholding certificate after significant household changes or when starting employment with a new employer.

Indiana's county residency rules should be considered separately from federal and state filing status.

## Federal Payroll Taxes for Indiana Employees

Indiana employees remain subject to applicable federal income tax withholding.

Your employer calculates federal withholding using taxable earnings, pay frequency and information from Form W-4.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages up to the 2026 annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare contributions apply at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers also generally withhold additional Medicare tax at 0.9% when covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) and the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for official federal withholding information.

## Indiana Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

An employee earning $65,000 annually would generally receive $2,500 every two weeks.

Assume this employee has one applicable Indiana personal exemption, is subject to Allen County tax and has no pre-tax employee deductions.

Approximately $2,196.99 remains before federal income tax withholding and other employee deductions.

This is a partial payroll example rather than a complete estimate of the employee's net income.

Enter your actual federal withholding information and benefit deductions into the calculator to estimate your complete paycheck.

## Indiana Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can calculate gross earnings using their hourly rate and working hours.

Suppose you earn $25 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 6 = $225

Total gross earnings:

$1,225

Federal taxes, Indiana income tax and applicable county taxes are then calculated from the appropriate taxable wage amounts.

Employees working in manufacturing, healthcare, transportation and logistics may receive additional compensation through shift differentials or overtime.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for eligibility requirements.

## Working Across Indiana State Borders

Indiana has reciprocal income tax agreements with Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.

These agreements can affect state income tax withholding on qualifying employee compensation.

However, state income tax reciprocity does not automatically eliminate Indiana county income tax obligations.

Employees who live outside Indiana and work within the state should confirm their eligibility and county tax circumstances with the relevant tax authority.

A standard Indiana paycheck calculation may not capture every multi-state employment arrangement.

## Comparing Salaries in Different Indiana Counties

When comparing job offers, examine both the advertised salary and applicable county income tax.

A higher county tax rate can reduce take-home pay even when two positions offer identical gross compensation.

Housing, commuting, healthcare benefits and employer retirement matching should also influence your decision.

Use the calculator to compare employment offers under their applicable withholding assumptions.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Indiana's income tax rate in 2026?

Indiana's individual state income tax rate is 2.95% in 2026. Applicable county income taxes are calculated separately.

### Which Indiana county income tax rate should I use?

For ordinary Indiana residents, the applicable county generally depends on where they lived on January 1 of the tax year. Qualifying nonresidents may use their principal Indiana employment location on that date.

### Do Indiana county income tax rates change during the year?

Yes. County rates may change in January or October. The calculator should use the official withholding schedule applicable to the payment date.
